documents.title: Your first capture
documents.summary: Use sim:0 to save your first image without connecting a camera.
documents.body: Start here Your first capture Use sim:0 to save your first image without connecting a camera. Install Capturefab . Open a terminal in a folder where you can save files. Run the commands below in order. capturefab list --kind sim capturefab info -c sim:0 capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o 'first-{seq}.png' capturefab inspect -c sim:0 info shows the simulator's image size, pixel format and available controls. Open the file named in the capture result to see the test pattern. In an empty folder, this is first-0001.png . The {seq} template picks the next free number. inspect measures brightness and sharpness and prints the path to a JPEG preview. To try a connected camera, run capturefab list . Replace sim:0 with the ID of your camera. If it does not appear, see Find cameras .

documents.title: Use Capturefab from an AI agent
documents.summary: Coding agents such as Claude Code or Codex drive cameras through the CLI and read its JSON results.
documents.body: Start here Use Capturefab from an AI agent Coding agents such as Claude Code or Codex drive cameras through the CLI and read its JSON results. Put capturefab on the agent's PATH . Give the agent agents.md or ask it to run capturefab schema . Ask it to capture one image from sim:0 in the task folder. For real hardware, give it a camera ID and specify which settings it can change. capturefab schema capturefab schema capture capturefab list --json capturefab inspect --json -c sim:0 --preview none capturefab capture --json -c sim:0 -o 'shots/{seq}.png' Use --json for structured results and errors . Read the exit code and error.code before deciding what to do next. Use schema COMMAND to look up the options, result fields and errors for one command. Command effects, from capturefab schema Effect Examples Suggested permission read list , info , features , get , inspect , jobs list , doctor , schema Allow for the task file_write capture , record , preset save Allow in the task's folder camera_write set , auto , preset apply , jobs stop Allow for the task's cameras disruptive exec , session start , session stop , serve , debug write Ask first Review flags as well as command names. --set , --auto and network --tune leave camera settings changed. inspect --preview PATH and debug xml -o FILE write to the specified paths. If your agent tool uses prefix rules, allow specific subcommands such as capturefab jobs list . A rule for capturefab jobs also matches capturefab jobs stop all . Use inspect --preview none for measurements alone. To give the agent a preview, use --preview PATH to save it in the task folder. Otherwise, capturefab doctor --json gives the default preview folder in inspect_dir .

documents.title: Install and verify
documents.summary: One command picks the build for this computer, checks its SHA-256 and installs capturefab for your account.
documents.body: Start here Install and verify One command picks the build for this computer, checks its SHA-256 and installs capturefab for your account. # macOS and Linux: ~/.local/share/capturefab, with the command in ~/.local/bin curl -fsSL https://capturefab.com/install.sh | sh # Windows PowerShell: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Capturefab, on your user PATH irm https://capturefab.com/install.ps1 | iex The installers use your account's permissions. You can read the macOS and Linux script or the Windows script before running it. To see which file the installer would use, run the saved script with --dry-run on macOS or Linux, or -DryRun on Windows. To download by hand, select a build for your operating system and processor. Use ARM64 for Apple silicon and x64 for Intel Macs. In the commands below, replace DOWNLOADED_FILE with the filename and EXPECTED_SHA256 with its checksum from the download page . # Linux echo "EXPECTED_SHA256 DOWNLOADED_FILE" | sha256sum -c # macOS echo "EXPECTED_SHA256 DOWNLOADED_FILE" | shasum -a 256 -c # Windows PowerShell if ((Get-FileHash .\DOWNLOADED_FILE -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -eq 'EXPECTED_SHA256') { 'OK: checksum matches' } else { 'MISMATCH: do not open this file' } Run the command for your operating system from the folder with the download. If the checksum matches, extract the archive. It contains capturefab or capturefab.exe , a README and the license files. Put capturefab on your PATH The Windows installer updates your user PATH . The macOS and Linux installer prints instructions if its command folder is missing from PATH . If you downloaded and extracted the archive by hand, use the commands for your operating system below. # macOS and Linux, from the extracted folder install -Dm755 ./capturefab ~/.local/bin/capturefab # Linux mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && cp ./capturefab ~/.local/bin/ # macOS # Windows PowerShell, from the extracted folder $dir = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Capturefab" New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $dir | Out-Null; Copy-Item -Recurse -Force .\* $dir $path = (Get-Item HKCU:\Environment).GetValue('Path', '', 'DoNotExpandEnvironmentNames') New-ItemProperty HKCU:\Environment Path -PropertyType ExpandString -Value "$path;$dir" -Force | Out-Null Open a new terminal and run capturefab --version . If it is not found on macOS or Linux, add export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" to ~/.zshrc or ~/.profile . Upgrade or uninstall Download the current installer again to upgrade. On macOS/Linux pass --upgrade or --uninstall ; on Windows save install.ps1 and run it with -Upgrade or -Uninstall . Add --dry-run ( -DryRun ) to preview. Custom installs need the same --prefix and --bin-dir ( -Prefix on Windows). Close running commands and sessions before uninstalling. Uninstall removes recognized release folders and their command link or PATH entries. Presets, saved sign-ins, caches and files outside those release folders stay. See the copyable upgrade/uninstall commands and agent installation instructions . A saved installer can uninstall offline; download a fresh script to install the latest version. First use: system prompts The first camera or network command can make your system ask for permission. These answers decide whether cameras appear. Prompts on first use System What to expect macOS macOS asks for Camera and Local Network access for the app you run the command in, such as Terminal, iTerm or your editor. Allow both: webcams need Camera, and GigE Vision, ONVIF and RTSP discovery need Local Network. To change them later, open System Settings › Privacy & Security › Camera or Local Network and turn that app on. A download from a browser is checked online by Gatekeeper the first time it runs. Windows A build marked Unsigned on the download page can show Windows protected your PC from SmartScreen. Check the SHA-256 first, then choose More info → Run anyway , or run Unblock-File .\capturefab.exe . The PowerShell installer needs neither. When Windows Defender Firewall asks, allow Capturefab on Private networks . GigE Vision and RTSP-over-UDP video arrive as inbound UDP; blocking it shows up as stream timeouts. USB3 Vision needs WinUSB. The camera's USB3 Vision interface must use the WinUSB driver. Close vendor camera software first. Use the vendor's driver tool if it can switch the camera to WinUSB; otherwise run Zadig , choose Options › List All Devices , select the camera's interface, choose WinUSB and select Replace Driver . Vendor software that needs its own driver cannot open the camera until you roll the driver back in Device Manager. Linux There are no prompts, but USB3 Vision cameras need device permissions and GigE Vision needs a larger socket receive buffer. Run capturefab doctor : it checks both and prints the command for each fix. The line computer guide explains the udev rule and net.core.rmem_max . Minimum operating system versions Build Minimum requirement macOS ARM64 macOS 11.0 macOS x64 macOS 10.15 Windows x64 Windows 10; Windows 11 on ARM can use x64 emulation. Windows ARM64 Windows 11 on ARM Linux x64 and ARM64 glibc 2.28; examples include Debian 10, RHEL 8 and Jetson Linux R34. These minimums also apply to the included FFmpeg executable. Windows builds need no Visual C++ redistributable. There is no 32-bit ARM build: on Debian-based Linux, dpkg --print-architecture must print arm64 for the ARM64 build. Release builds need no separate Aravis, FFmpeg, libusb or vendor SDK. capturefab --version capturefab doctor # Optional: verify GitHub build provenance gh attestation verify DOWNLOADED_FILE --repo capturefab/capturefab

documents.title: Upgrade from the desktop app
documents.summary: Capturefab is now a command-line tool. Releases up to 0.5.0 were a desktop app with a CLI inside.
documents.body: Start here Upgrade from the desktop app Capturefab is now a command-line tool. Releases up to 0.5.0 were a desktop app with a CLI inside. The desktop window, browser client, built-in AI assistant, datasets, camera hubs, document scanners, workflow files and update checks are gone. Cameras, captures, recordings and saved sign-ins work as before through the commands on this page, with new names and a new JSON contract: read the command reference before you reuse a script. macOS: run the install script. It replaces a ~/.local/bin/capturefab link into Capturefab.app and says what it changed; the app itself stays until you delete it. If your shell profile adds /Applications/Capturefab.app/Contents/MacOS to PATH , remove that line. Linux: the install script removes the launcher entry and icons an earlier install added. Earlier versions stay in ~/.local/share/capturefab until you delete them. Windows: the install script removes the Start menu shortcut an earlier install added and keeps one Capturefab folder on your PATH . Files the desktop app kept, such as its preferences, saved hubs, destinations and dataset files, are not read any more; delete them when you no longer need them. Saved camera sign-ins stay in the OS credential store and keep working. To keep using the desktop app, keep version 0.5.0 and skip the update it offers; its downloads remain at https://capturefab.com/download/v0.5.0/ , with each file listed in releases.json .

documents.title: Find cameras
documents.summary: list searches for connected cameras and prints an ID you can pass to -c .
documents.body: Cameras Find cameras list searches for connected cameras and prints an ID you can pass to -c . capturefab list capturefab list --kind gige,u3v --timeout 3s capturefab list --kind webcam capturefab --json list Use --kind to filter the search. Screen sources and simulators appear only when you ask for screen or sim . Use --timeout to give GigE Vision and ONVIF cameras more time to reply. If a search fails for one connection type, read warnings in the JSON result. In scripts, pass the camera ID with -c . A unique serial number or a GigE camera’s IPv4 address also works. If you omit -c and Capturefab finds several cameras, it can prompt you to choose in a terminal. An ambiguous selector returns camera_ambiguous . A GigE camera needs a reachable address on a wired adapter's subnet; capturefab network checks the path. USB3 Vision needs operating system access: the udev rule on Linux, an available IOKit interface on macOS and WinUSB on Windows. Read the camera requirements and limits .

documents.title: Camera selectors
documents.summary: -c takes a list ID, a serial, an IP address, a stream URL, a file or a simulator.
documents.body: Cameras Camera selectors -c takes a list ID, a serial, an IP address, a stream URL, a file or a simulator. Selector examples Source Selector GigE Vision or USB3 Vision camera gige:00c0df123456 , a u3v: ID, a serial number or 192.168.1.20 Webcam or capture card avfoundation:Camera Name (macOS), v4l2:/dev/video0 (Linux), dshow:video=Camera Name (Windows); add ?size=1280x720&fps=30 to ask for a mode Network stream rtsp://cam.local/stream , rtsps://… , srt://… , http(s)://… ONVIF camera onvif://cam.local or onvif:http://HOST/onvif/device_service Video or image file a path, such as clip.mkv Simulator sim:0 , sim:1 , sim:line , sim:depth , sim:microscope , sim:thermal , sim:replay:PATH Quote selectors that contain spaces, ? or & . For supported password-protected cameras, use login add to store credentials outside the script. capturefab capture -c 'avfoundation:Camera Name?size=1280x720' -o webcam.png capturefab features -c v4l2:/dev/video0 VideoMode capturefab capture -c rtsp://cam.local/stream -n 5 -o snapshots/ capturefab capture -c clip.mkv -n 100 -o frames/

documents.title: Simulated cameras
documents.summary: Built-in cameras for learning, scripting and tests without hardware.
documents.body: Cameras Simulated cameras Built-in cameras for learning, scripting and tests without hardware. sim:0 and other numbered simulators generate a moving pattern. They support exposure, gain, frame rate, region, several pixel formats and triggers. Use sim:line , sim:depth , sim:microscope or sim:thermal to try a different camera type. Use sim:replay:PATH to replay a video, an image or a folder of media files. capturefab inspect -c sim:0 --set exposure=40ms capturefab capture -c sim:0 -c sim:1 -o 'multi/{camera}-{seq}.png' capturefab capture -c sim:replay:/data/clip.mp4 -n 100 -o replay-frames/ Simulator settings stay in the runtime folder between commands. Use capture --set to change settings before saving an image. See the simulator guide for replay and trigger options.

documents.title: Read and change settings
documents.summary: Use info to see what a camera supports. Use get and set to read and change its settings.
documents.body: Cameras Read and change settings Use info to see what a camera supports. Use get and set to read and change its settings. capturefab info -c sim:0 capturefab features -c sim:0 Trigger capturefab features -c sim:0 'Exposure*' --all capturefab get -c sim:0 exposure gain ExposureTime 'TriggerMode[FrameStart]' capturefab set -c sim:0 exposure=5ms gain=3 capturefab set -c sim:0 roi=0,0,320,240 fps=20 --dry-run capturefab exec -c sim:0 'TriggerSoftware[FrameStart]' Use portable controls such as exposure , gain , fps and roi when the camera supports them. For a GenICam feature, use the name from features , such as ExposureTime . A selector in brackets, such as TriggerMode[FrameStart] , chooses which value to read or change. Quote names with brackets so the shell passes them as written. Use set --dry-run to see the planned writes in order. After a write, the result shows the value read back from the camera. A camera can round a value to its supported increment. If a write fails, Capturefab tries to restore the earlier values. Read error.details.rollback to see which values it restored and which it could not restore. For an unknown feature, look for details.did_you_mean . For an out-of-range value, look for details.nearest . features shows common features by default. Use a name pattern, --category or --all to see more. exec runs a command feature such as UserSetSave[UserSet1] .

documents.title: Measure exposure and focus
documents.summary: inspect measures a fresh frame and writes a small preview, without saving a capture.
documents.body: Cameras Measure exposure and focus inspect measures a fresh frame and writes a small preview, without saving a capture. capturefab inspect -c sim:0 capturefab inspect -c sim:0 --set exposure=20ms --region 0.25,0.25,0.5,0.5 capturefab inspect -c sim:0 --keep 5m --preview none capturefab --json inspect -c sim:0 -v --preview none capturefab watch -c sim:0 --show --for 5s Read verdict for conditions such as dark or clipped_high . One frame can have more than one condition. Read exposure for brightness and counts of pixels at black or full scale. When present, suggest gives an exposure to try. Compare focus.sharpness across frames from the same camera and scene. Higher values indicate sharper edges. Use -v for a histogram and more focus measures. Use --set to change settings before measuring. Use --region X,Y,W,H to measure part of the frame. Each number is a fraction of the full width or height. The JPEG preview’s longest edge is 768 pixels by default. Use --size to change it, or --preview none to skip the preview. Use --for 10s --every 200ms to measure a series and get the sharpest frame’s results. For live measurements, use watch . Add --show to see frames in a compatible terminal, or --json for one JSON line per measurement. Use --fresh N to skip extra frames before measuring. If verdict contains not_settled , the camera’s automatic exposure was still changing when --warmup ended.

documents.title: Auto exposure
documents.summary: auto settles exposure and gain, then holds them.
documents.body: Cameras Auto exposure auto settles exposure and gain, then holds them. capturefab auto -c sim:0 capturefab auto -c sim:0 --timeout 10s capturefab auto -c sim:0 --off capturefab capture -c sim:0 --auto -o settled.png auto uses the camera’s auto exposure when available. Capturefab adjusts exposure and gain itself if the camera has no auto mode or if you set --region or --max-exposure . Read settled even when the command exits 0. If present, limited_by names the limit that affected the result. Use --off to turn off automatic exposure, gain and white balance while keeping their current values. Use --continuous to keep adjusting exposure. Capturefab’s own continuous loop runs only in a session. A camera without exposure control or one that waits for external triggers can return unsupported .

documents.title: Triggered capture
documents.summary: With a software trigger, capture fires it; with a hardware trigger, it waits for the line.
documents.body: Cameras Triggered capture With a software trigger, capture fires it; with a hardware trigger, it waits for the line. capturefab capture -c 'sim:0?line0=every:500ms' --set trigger=software -o 'software-{seq}.png' capturefab set -c 'sim:0?line0=every:500ms' trigger=line0:rising --keep 5m capturefab capture -c 'sim:0?line0=every:500ms' -o 'part-{seq}.png' --timeout 30s capturefab set -c 'sim:0?line0=every:500ms' trigger=off sim:0?line0=every:500ms supplies a Line0 trigger every 500 ms. Plain sim:0 does not supply those signals. The trigger setting stays in effect for later commands. Set trigger=off to return to free-running capture. For a hardware trigger, capture waits up to --timeout per frame. The default wait is at least 5s . If no trigger arrives in time, it exits 4 with trigger_timeout . For a long wait, use --timeout none --background and follow the job ID with jobs .

documents.title: Capture images
documents.summary: capture saves one frame, a burst, a time lapse or a delayed capture, and never overwrites a file.
documents.body: Capture & record Capture images capture saves one frame, a burst, a time lapse or a delayed capture, and never overwrites a file. capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o shot.png capturefab capture -c sim:0 -n 10 -o frames/ capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o shot.jpg --quality 85 capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o frames/ -f raw capturefab capture -c sim:0 --set exposure=20ms --set gain=6 -o bright.png capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o shot2.png --dry-run Image formats Format Use png The default. Saves high-bit-depth monochrome frames as 16-bit grayscale. Saves color and Bayer frames as 8-bit RGB. jpg Use --quality from 1 to 100. The default is 90 for encoded JPEGs. For Motion JPEG input, Capturefab can save the source JPEG directly. Look for "passthrough": true . To encode it again, set --quality . raw Saves the frame buffer at its original bit depth. For FFmpeg sources, this is the decoded frame. A file such as shot.raw.json describes the pixel format, dimensions and layout of shot.raw . See the pixel format table for supported conversions. The result gives the output bit_depth . If the file uses fewer bits than the input, it also gives source_bits . The output extension sets the format. Use -f to choose a format when there is no extension. End a new folder path with / to save numbered files there. If you omit -o , Capturefab saves to the current folder. Use -o - to write one image to stdout. With --json , the result or error goes to stderr in this mode. Use --timeout to set the wait per frame. The default is at least 5s and can be longer for slow cameras. Use --set or --auto to adjust the camera before capture. A fixed filename that already exists returns exists unless you pass --on-exists number . Use {seq} to choose the next free number automatically. Repeat -c to request frames from several cameras together. A foreground result has one entry per camera in cameras . skew_ms measures how far apart the first frames arrived. For synchronized exposures, use a shared hardware trigger. With --background , the result has a jobs list instead. capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o measured.png --inspect --manifest shots.jsonl capturefab capture -c sim:0 --set exposure=20ms --fresh 2 -o after.png capturefab capture -c sim:0 -n 100 -o 'scratch/{seq}.raw' --sync none Use time for the frame’s host timestamp and device_ts_ns for the camera’s own clock when available. For a burst, read fps , gaps and consecutive to see how the capture ran. Use --fresh N to skip extra frames after a change. Use --inspect to measure the last frame. Use --manifest FILE to append a JSON line for each saved file with its path, SHA-256, settings and tags. The default sync writes each capture to disk before reporting it. Use --sync none for temporary images you can afford to lose after a power failure.

documents.title: Name files and tag captures
documents.summary: Templates in -o build file names from the camera, time, sequence and your tags.
documents.body: Capture & record Name files and tag captures Templates in -o build file names from the camera, time, sequence and your tags. capturefab capture -c sim:0 -n 10 -o 'parts/{date}/{tag:part}-{seq:4}.png' --tag part=A-100 --tag station=3 capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o 'labels/{tag:label}/{seq:5}.png' --tag label=defect capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o shot.png --on-exists number Output placeholders Placeholder Value {camera} The camera's model and serial, safe for file names {serial} The serial number {seq} , {seq:N} 1, 2, 3 …, padded to N digits (4 by default) {frame} Frame number within this capture, starting at 000001 {time} The time, such as 20261031-142233.123 {date} The date, such as 2026-10-31 {datetime} Date and time to the second, such as 20261031-142233 {tag:KEY} The value of --tag KEY=VALUE {ext} png , jpg or raw Capturefab saves tags and camera settings in PNG and JPEG metadata. Relative paths start in the folder where you run the command, even when a session writes the files. Use --on-exists number to add -0001 , -0002 and so on when a fixed name is already in use. See the plant-floor guide for naming and tagging examples.

documents.title: Time lapses and delayed captures
documents.summary: --every spaces frames, --for or -n bounds them, and --at or --in delays the start.
documents.body: Capture & record Time lapses and delayed captures --every spaces frames, --for or -n bounds them, and --at or --in delays the start. capturefab capture -c sim:0 -n 3 --every 2s -o 'lapse/{seq:5}.png' capturefab capture -c sim:0 --in 5s -o 'later-{seq}.png' # Schedule a capture for 06:00 local time capturefab capture -c sim:0 --at 06:00 -o 'morning-{seq}.png' --background Give durations a unit, such as 250ms , 2s or 1h30m . Use --at HH:MM for a time on the local clock, or pass an RFC 3339 timestamp with its time zone. Use --background to return a job ID while a session runs the capture. In JSON, read job.id . Pass that ID to jobs wait or jobs stop . See sessions and jobs .

documents.title: Record and stream video
documents.summary: record writes video to a file or streams it to a server through the bundled FFmpeg.
documents.body: Capture & record Record and stream video record writes video to a file or streams it to a server through the bundled FFmpeg. capturefab record -c sim:0 -o 'clip-{seq}.mp4' --for 5s capturefab record -c sim:0 -o 'lossless-{seq}.mkv' --codec ffv1 --for 5s capturefab record -c sim:0 -o 'limited-{seq}.mp4' --bitrate 4M --max-size 2G --for 5s To stream video, start a receiver such as MediaMTX first. Use the URL for the protocol your receiver accepts. capturefab record -c sim:0 -o rtsp://localhost:8554/cam --for 10s capturefab record -c sim:0 -o 'srt://localhost:8890?streamid=publish:cam' --for 10s For a local file, use .mkv , .mp4 , .mov , .ts or .webm . Choose a container that supports the codec. Use --codec ffv1 in an MKV file for lossless video. For Bayer input, it saves the mosaic as gray samples. When Capturefab encodes H.264, it tries hardware first and can use libx264 from the bundled FFmpeg. HEVC and AV1 encoding need a supported hardware encoder. On supported systems, Capturefab can copy H.264 or HEVC video directly into the output. Look for "encoder":"copy" . A recording can start at the previous key frame. To encode instead, set --fps , --bitrate or a different codec. Windows always encodes. Use --for or --max-size to limit a recording. To stop a foreground recording, push Ctrl-C. Read ended and finalized in the JSON result to see how it ended and whether Capturefab finished writing the file.

documents.title: Save and restore settings
documents.summary: A preset keeps a camera's settings on this computer and restores them as one change.
documents.body: Capture & record Save and restore settings A preset keeps a camera's settings on this computer and restores them as one change. capturefab preset save bench -c sim:0 --note 'ring light 60%' capturefab preset list capturefab preset apply bench -c sim:0 --dry-run capturefab preset apply bench -c sim:0 capturefab preset export bench -o bench.json capturefab preset import bench.json --name bench2 Use apply --dry-run to review changes before applying them. The plan marks disruptive changes such as triggering or I/O settings. Use --strict to stop if a saved value does not fit the camera. Use --allow-other-model to apply compatible settings to another model. If a write fails, Capturefab tries to restore the earlier settings. To save the applied settings as the camera’s power-on defaults, use --persist on cameras that support user sets.

documents.title: Password-protected cameras
documents.summary: login add saves a stream's user name and password in the OS credential store.
documents.body: Capture & record Password-protected cameras login add saves a stream's user name and password in the OS credential store. printf '%s\n' "$PASSWORD" | capturefab login add rtsp://cam.local/stream --user admin --password-stdin capturefab login list capturefab onvif resolve cam.local capturefab login rm rtsp://cam.local/stream Use a camera address without credentials. Supply the password on stdin with --password-stdin , or set CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA_PASSWORD . In this example, PASSWORD is a shell variable you set before running the command. By default, login add verifies the sign-in before saving it. Use --no-check to skip the connection. Later commands for that address use the saved credentials. If credentials are missing or the camera rejects them, look for auth_required or auth_rejected . Capturefab passes RTSP credentials to FFmpeg in its input URL. On systems where other users can read process arguments, they can see those credentials. RTSP Basic authentication also exposes credentials on an unencrypted connection. Use rtsps:// if the camera supports it.

documents.title: Sessions, --keep and jobs
documents.summary: A session keeps cameras open between commands and runs background jobs.
documents.body: Automate Sessions, --keep and jobs A session keeps cameras open between commands and runs background jobs. Run a capture in a named session capturefab session start --name bench -c sim:1 --live capturefab capture --session bench -c sim:1 -n 3 --every 2s -o 'bench/{seq}.png' --background capturefab session status bench Replace JOB_ID below with the ID from the capture result. capturefab jobs wait JOB_ID --timeout 10s capturefab session stop bench Capturefab normally holds a camera in the auto session for 60 seconds after a command. Use --keep DUR to change that time. Use --keep 0 to avoid starting a warm session. Use --no-session to bypass existing sessions as well. session start runs a named session in the background with a default idle limit of 30 minutes. Use --session NAME to select it. --live keeps frames flowing between commands. For a service manager, use serve --name NAME to run the session in the foreground. See the line computer guide . Use jobs list --running to see active jobs. jobs wait exits 0 when all requested jobs succeed. It returns a failed job’s exit code, or exits 4 if the wait times out. Use jobs stop JOB_ID to stop a specific job and keep the files it saved. Stopping a session interrupts its active jobs. See CLI workflows for examples of how to combine these commands in scripts.

documents.title: JSON results and exit codes
documents.summary: Use --json to read command results and errors from a script.
documents.body: Automate JSON results and exit codes Use --json to read command results and errors from a script. capturefab --json get -c sim:0 ExposureTime 'TriggerMode[FrameStart]' capturefab schema capturefab schema set capturefab completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_capturefab Most commands write one JSON result to stdout on exit 0. A failure returns a nonzero exit code and a JSON error with code , message and optional hint and details . Logs and progress go to stderr. Set CAPTUREFAB_JSON=1 to make JSON the default. Some commands use different output. watch --json emits one JSON line per measurement. Batch shell --json emits one line per command. capture -o - reserves stdout for the image and sends the JSON to stderr. Top-level help and version output remain text. Process exit codes Code Category Examples of error.code 0 ok — 1 failed failed , exists , feature_locked , incomplete 2 usage or input usage , invalid_duration , feature_not_found , out_of_range , invalid_choice , camera_ambiguous 3 unavailable camera_not_found , camera_busy , permission_denied , disconnected , ffmpeg_missing , auth_required 4 timeout frame_timeout , trigger_timeout , timeout 5 unsupported unsupported 6 storage full storage_full 130 interrupted (143 SIGTERM, 129 SIGHUP) interrupted , with partial results in details The command reference lists options, result fields and error codes. The site generates it from capturefab schema and command help.

documents.title: GigE network checks
documents.summary: network checks how each GigE camera is reached; --tune shares bandwidth between cameras.
documents.body: Automate GigE network checks network checks how each GigE camera is reached; --tune shares bandwidth between cameras. capturefab network capturefab network --tune -c gige:00c0df123456 -c gige:00c0df654321 Run network to see which adapter reaches each GigE camera. It reports the adapter’s IPv4 address, MTU and link speed when available. Use --tune to set camera packet delays or throughput limits when cameras share a link. Tuning changes camera settings only.

documents.title: Check this computer
documents.summary: doctor reports problems with camera access, FFmpeg and local folders. It gives a fix when one is available.
documents.body: Reference Check this computer doctor reports problems with camera access, FFmpeg and local folders. It gives a fix when one is available. capturefab doctor capturefab --json doctor Use capturefab doctor --json to see the build’s features and the FFmpeg it uses in ffmpeg . Look in folders for the runtime, state and cache paths. Look in inspect_dir for the preview path. Use jpeg and hwdec to see whether JPEG encoders and hardware video decoders passed local tests.

documents.title: Troubleshooting
documents.summary: Read error.code and error.hint first; doctor checks the computer.
documents.body: Reference Troubleshooting Read error.code and error.hint first; doctor checks the computer. capturefab doctor capturefab --json list capturefab session list capturefab -v info -c sim:0 A camera is missing or cannot connect Read the warnings of list and use the camera's full ID. For GigE, network checks reachability on its subnet. For USB3 Vision, check operating system access: doctor prints the Linux udev rule, and on Windows the camera must use WinUSB . On macOS, a camera at a correct address that reports no route to host can mean Local Network access was denied to your terminal app. camera_busy: another process holds the camera A session or another command has the camera open; error.details.held_by names it when known. Run the command through that session ( --session NAME ), wait for its job, or stop it with jobs stop or session stop . frame_timeout or trigger_timeout Make sure the camera streams and that its trigger can supply frames: info shows the trigger. Raise --timeout for slow sources, or set trigger=off . For GigE, packet loss looks like timeouts: check the receive buffer and network . A setting is locked or rejected feature_locked names the setting that locks it in details.locked_by ; change that first. Some features can change only while the camera is not streaming. set --dry-run shows what a change would write. A frame's pixel format is unsupported Choose another PixelFormat the camera offers, or capture raw to keep the bytes as they are. The pixel format table lists the supported formats. A stream, video file or encoder fails doctor shows whether FFmpeg runs. Make sure a receiving server is up and reachable. hevc and av1 need a working hardware encoder; h264 always has libx264. A development build can use CAPTUREFAB_FFMPEG=/absolute/path/to/ffmpeg . An SSH shell cannot find a session a service started Without XDG_RUNTIME_DIR , a Linux service uses /run/user/<uid> only when its user lingers. Run sudo loginctl enable-linger USER and give the service Wants= and After=user@<uid>.service . doctor in the SSH shell says where a service keeps its sessions. Capture stops with storage_full A write would have taken the disk below the free space Capturefab leaves for the system: 1% of the disk, at least 512 MiB and at most 20 GiB. error.details gives the path and its free_bytes . Free space or capture to another disk; CAPTUREFAB_MIN_FREE (bytes or a size such as 2G , 0 for none) changes the floor. Capturefab never deletes files to make room. For a bug report, include capturefab --version , the operating system, the camera type, the exact command and its JSON output, and capturefab --json doctor . Remove private addresses and names before you share them.

documents.title: Environment variables and folders
documents.summary: Variables set defaults for flags and move the folders Capturefab uses.
documents.body: Reference Environment variables and folders Variables set defaults for flags and move the folders Capturefab uses. Environment variables Variable Purpose CAPTUREFAB_JSON=1 --json for every command CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA The default -c CAPTUREFAB_SESSION The default --session ; --no-session overrides it CAPTUREFAB_KEEP The default --keep ( 60s ); 0 turns the warm default off CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA_PASSWORD The password for login add without --password-stdin CAPTUREFAB_FFMPEG An absolute path to an FFmpeg executable to use instead of the bundled one CAPTUREFAB_SESSION_DIR One folder for sessions, presets and the sign-in index; for isolated runs and tests use a private (mode 0700) folder, such as one from mktemp -d , or a path that does not exist yet CAPTUREFAB_STATE_DIR The folder for presets, the sign-in index, job records and session logs CAPTUREFAB_CACHE_DIR The folder for the extracted FFmpeg, encoder probes and GenICam XML CAPTUREFAB_MIN_FREE The free space a write leaves on its disk, in bytes or a size such as 2G ; 0 turns the floor off CAPTUREFAB_THREADS At most this many image processing threads CAPTUREFAB_IMAGES How watch --show draws frames: kitty , iterm , truecolor , 256 or none CAPTUREFAB_MAX_CAMERAS Cameras one session may hold, 1–64 (default 16) CAPTUREFAB_GVSP_SCATTER=0 GigE Vision packets are received whole and copied into their frames, rather than received straight into them CAPTUREFAB_JPEG The JPEG encoder: auto (the default: Apple's JPEG engine on macOS for color frames of at least 512K pixels at the default quality, and on Linux nvJPEG or VA-API for frames of at least 512K pixels, where it is faster and as accurate as libjpeg-turbo, checked beside the first frame of each size, which libjpeg-turbo writes), cpu (libjpeg-turbo), videotoolbox , nvjpeg or vaapi ; a named engine that is missing or fails its accuracy check is exit 3. nvJPEG and VA-API run in a helper process the camera worker starts, which reads frames from the shared memory the camera wrote them to; one that crashes or stops answering is ended, and under auto libjpeg-turbo takes over, with a warning on stderr, while a named one fails the still with exit 3. CAPTUREFAB_CUDA_LIB_DIR A folder holding the CUDA runtime and nvJPEG libraries, tried before the loader's paths CAPTUREFAB_VAAPI_DEVICE The DRM render node VA-API JPEG encoding uses, instead of the first /dev/dri/renderD* that encodes JPEG CAPTUREFAB_HWDEC Hardware decoding of H.264, HEVC and other compressed video: auto (the default: compressed streams and webcams in a session, the warm one included, whose decoder runs on between commands; files and --no-session commands get their one frame sooner in software), none , or a method such as videotoolbox , cuda , vulkan or d3d11va , used for files and --no-session too; one this FFmpeg lacks or that fails its probe is exit 3. Motion JPEG is decoded with libjpeg-turbo whatever it says. A session's cameras keep the CAPTUREFAB_JPEG , CAPTUREFAB_HWDEC and CAPTUREFAB_FFMPEG the session started with, the warm auto session included: stop it with capturefab session stop auto , or use --no-session , for a command to use other values. A command's own CAPTUREFAB_MIN_FREE raises the free-space floor for the files a session writes for it, but does not lower the floor the session started with. The runtime folder holds active sessions. The state folder holds presets, sign-in records and job history. The cache folder holds extracted FFmpeg and cached probes. Run capturefab doctor --json and read folders for the paths and fallbacks. See the embedded and read-only hosts guide for defaults and permission rules.

documents.title: Build, architecture and licensing
documents.summary: Capturefab runs each camera in its own worker process. It runs FFmpeg as a separate executable.
documents.body: Reference Build, architecture and licensing Capturefab runs each camera in its own worker process. It runs FFmpeg as a separate executable. Capturefab implements GigE Vision, USB3 Vision and GenICam in Rust. The camera worker belongs to the command or to a session. This separation helps other camera workers continue when one fails. Capturefab uses FFmpeg for webcams, streams, media files and video encoding. Build from source Install a stable Rust toolchain, a C compiler and CMake. On x86, also install NASM for libjpeg-turbo. Download the release source archive . Replace VERSION below with the version you downloaded. tar -xzf capturefab-VERSION-source.tar.gz cd capturefab-VERSION cargo --config .cargo/vendor-config.toml build --release --offline --locked target/release/capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o first.png To bundle FFmpeg, build it separately and set CAPTUREFAB_FFMPEG_BINARY when building Capturefab. At run time Capturefab looks for CAPTUREFAB_FFMPEG , the bundled copy, a copy next to capturefab , then a copy on PATH . See the FFmpeg build guide . The default features are usb (USB3 Vision), jpeg (libjpeg-turbo), videotoolbox (Apple's JPEG engine on macOS), nvjpeg and vaapi (the GPU JPEG encoders on Linux, whose libraries are loaded at run time in a helper process, so a build needs no SDK), keychain (the OS credential store for login ) and shell (line editing in capturefab shell ); --no-default-features builds without them, and doctor --json lists what a build has. Licensing and release provenance Capturefab uses the MIT license. The embedded FFmpeg is GPLv3 with x264, SRT, OpenSSL and zlib; capturefab licenses prints both notices. See the FFmpeg build and compliance guide . The downloads page shows how to verify each file, and the release manifest lists files, checksums and build metadata.

documents.title: JSON results, exit codes and errors
documents.summary: Read JSON results and progress lines. Use exit codes to handle errors.
documents.body: JSON results, exit codes and errors Read JSON results and progress lines. Use exit codes to handle errors. --json or CAPTUREFAB_JSON=1 usually writes one result line to stdout. A failure returns error with code , message and optional hint and details . Use the exit code for the category and error.code for the specific reason. watch --json and shell --json emit NDJSON. With capture --json -o - , image bytes go to stdout and JSON goes to stderr. --progress sends JSON progress to stderr. NDJSON means one JSON object per line. --help and --version print text. Use --progress with capture , record or jobs wait to follow job progress. Each line has a progress object. Keys use snake_case , with units in names such as exposure_us . Timestamps use RFC 3339 UTC. Missing fields are omitted. A result can include up to 10 distinct warnings. Capturefab redacts credentials in camera URLs. Run capturefab schema COMMAND for arguments, result fields and errors. This reference uses that output and the CLI help. The contract version is 1 . Exit codes Exit code Category 0 ok 1 failed 2 usage or input 3 unavailable 4 timeout 5 unsupported 6 storage full 130 interrupted (143 SIGTERM, 129 SIGHUP) Error codes in error.code Code Exit Meaning exists 1 the output exists (never overwritten); details.path failed 1 the operation failed feature_locked 1 another setting locks the feature now; see details.locked_by incomplete 1 fewer results than requested; see details camera_ambiguous 2 several cameras match; pick one of details.candidates with -c feature_not_found 2 no such feature or control; see details.did_you_mean invalid_choice 2 not one of details.choices invalid_duration 2 not a valid duration (see grammars.duration) not_writable 2 the feature is read-only out_of_range 2 outside the feature's range; details {feature,value,min,max,inc,nearest,unit} usage 2 invalid arguments or input auth_rejected 3 the camera refused the sign-in auth_required 3 the camera needs a sign-in; run login add camera_busy 3 another process or job holds the camera; details.held_by when known camera_not_found 3 no camera matches; details.candidates lists what answered disconnected 3 the camera went away ffmpeg_missing 3 FFmpeg could not be found or started permission_denied 3 the OS refused access; see hint session_not_found 3 no running session has that name unavailable 3 the camera, stream or service cannot be reached worker_crashed 3 the camera worker process died frame_timeout 4 no frame arrived in time timeout 4 the operation did not finish in time trigger_timeout 4 a triggered camera got no trigger in time; details.trigger unsupported 5 the camera or this build cannot do that storage_full 6 disk full or below CAPTUREFAB_MIN_FREE; details {path,free_bytes?} interrupted 130 stopped by a signal; details hold partial results

documents.title: Global options, cameras and sessions
documents.summary: Choose a camera, control session use and see what commands can change.
documents.body: Global options, cameras and sessions Choose a camera, control session use and see what commands can change. Put global options before or after the command. Global options Option Meaning Environment --json Print JSON results and errors CAPTUREFAB_JSON -q , --quiet Hide status and notes. Still report errors and explicit --progress output — -v , --verbose More detail on stderr, including camera worker logs — --session NAME Use this running session (session start or serve --name NAME) CAPTUREFAB_SESSION --no-session Bypass sessions for camera commands — -h , --help Print help (see more with '--help') — -V , --version Print version — Use -c CAM or CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA . By default, use the session's only camera or the only camera discovered. Discovery for this default excludes simulators and screens. Use --session NAME to choose a session. Otherwise, commands reuse a matching session. Most camera commands keep the camera open in auto for 60s after use. --keep 0 can reuse a session. Use --no-session to bypass sessions. --no-session overrides CAPTUREFAB_SESSION and CAPTUREFAB_KEEP . It conflicts with an explicit --session , --background or positive --keep . capture and record normally wait for the job. --background returns a job to follow with jobs wait ID . Each command lists its default effect. Look for options that add a file or camera write in the argument table. read Reads data. It can write a temporary preview. file_write Can write files or update saved data on this computer. camera_write Can change camera settings or jobs. disruptive Can hold cameras, stop streams or run camera commands.

documents.title: Selectors, names, durations and templates
documents.summary: See what to type for camera selectors, feature names, durations and output templates.
documents.body: Selectors, names, durations and templates See what to type for camera selectors, feature names, durations and output templates. Accepted forms Value Form duration Add a unit, as in 250ms , 1.5s or 1h30m . Use 0 where allowed. Some waits accept none for an unlimited wait name Use Feature , Feature[Selector=Value,…] or Feature[Value] for one selector. Controls include exposure , gain , fps , roi , format , trigger , auto_exposure and auto_wb selector Camera ID from list , serial, IPv4, stream URL such as rtsp://HOST/PATH , onvif://HOST , file path, sim:N[?drop=0..0.5&line0=every:DUR] or sim:replay:PATH template Capture names accept {camera} , {serial} , {seq} , {seq:N} , {frame} , {time} , {date} , {datetime} , {tag:KEY} and {ext} In a shell, put quotes around names, selectors and templates with special characters. For example, use 'TriggerMode[FrameStart]' or 'frames/{seq}.png' . Use an existing folder or end the path with a separator to save numbered files. Use {seq:N} to pad the number to N digits, from 1 to 9. Use --on-exists number to add a number when a fixed capture filename already exists.

documents.title: Capture, record and measure
documents.summary: Save images and video. Measure brightness and focus or set auto exposure.
documents.body: Capture, record and measure Save images and video. Measure brightness and focus or set auto exposure. capturefab capture Save an image, burst, time lapse or scheduled capture without overwriting files. Effect: file_write . capturefab capture arguments Argument or option Meaning Details -c , --camera CAM Camera ID, serial, IP address, stream URL, file path or simulator (sim:0). Repeat for more cameras env CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA ; repeatable -o , --output PATH Save to a file, template or folder. Use - for one image on stdout. By default, save in the current folder as {camera}-{time}-{seq}.{ext} — -n , --count N Frames to save, 1..100000 — --every DUR Time between frames of a time lapse, with -n or --for — --for DUR How long a time lapse runs, with --every — --at TIME Start at the next local HH:MM[:SS], or an RFC 3339 timestamp — --in DUR Start after a delay — -f , --format FORMAT Image format when -o has no extension: png (default; 16-bit for Mono10..Mono16), jpg or raw (the exact bytes, with NAME.json beside) one of png , jpg , raw --quality 1-100 JPEG quality, 1..100 (default 90; without it, a Motion JPEG source's own JPEG is stored as it is) — --set NAME=VALUE Change settings first, as one atomic change (as set does); repeatable repeatable; effect camera_write --auto Settle exposure and gain first, then hold them (as auto does) effect camera_write --inspect Measure the last frame as inspect does, and preview it: the result's inspect block — --tag KEY=VALUE Tag the files: {tag:KEY} in -o, and in each image's metadata; repeatable repeatable --timeout DUR How long to wait for each frame (default: 5s, or 3 exposures and frame periods when longer); none waits for a trigger until stopped — --fresh N Frames to let pass after the first one exposed after the last settings change, 0..10 default 0 --warmup DUR How long a camera that sets its own exposure (a webcam, or ExposureAuto=Continuous; a network stream is already running) may take to settle after it starts; 0 takes frames at once default 2s --on-exists ON_EXISTS When a file name without {seq} exists: fail, or number (-0001, -0002, ...) one of fail , number ; default fail --manifest FILE Append one JSON line per saved file (path, time, size, SHA-256, settings, tags) to this file — --sync SYNC file: each file reaches the disk before it is reported; none: skip that, for scratch captures one of file , none ; default file --background Leave the capture running in a session; print its job once it is armed or has saved its first frame (up to --timeout; with --timeout none, after 2s without waiting for a trigger) — --progress Report progress on stderr, also without a terminal: a JSON line {progress:{job,camera,kind,state,saved,planned?,bytes?,elapsed_s,left_s?,next_s?}} as the job changes, at least each second — --keep DUR Keep the camera open in a session after use (default 60s). Use 0 to reuse an open session or run without one env CAPTUREFAB_KEEP --dry-run Show the camera, files, settings and timing; capture nothing — capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o shot.png capturefab capture -c sim:0 -n 10 -o frames/ capturefab capture -c sim:0 --every 10s --for 1h -o 'lapse/{seq}.jpg' --background capturefab capture -c sim:0 -o - > frame.png capturefab capture JSON result Field Type and meaning after_change true — frames exposed before the camera's last settings change were let pass auto true — with --dry-run and --auto bandwidth_mbps float — with -c repeated, for GigE cameras that share a host network interface: the rate this one was paced to, its share of the interface (a warning when it could not be paced) bit_depth int — bits per sample in the files: 16 for PNG of Mono10..Mono16 (samples at the top bits, sBIT says how many count), every bit for raw, else 8 bytes int — with -o -: the image's size camera string — camera ID cameras [{camera,files,count,truncated?,width,height,pixel_format,bit_depth,source_bits?,settings,time,device_ts_ns?,frames,dropped,incomplete?,resent?,duration_s?,fps?,first_id?,last_id?,gaps?,consecutive?,after_change?,warmup_ms?,settled?,bandwidth_mbps?,warnings?,inspect?,dry_run?,output?,format?,every_s?,first_at?,ends_at?,auto?}] — with -c repeated: one result per camera; in error details, a failed camera's {camera,error,files?,truncated?,job?} consecutive bool — a burst's frames follow one another with no frame missing count int — frames saved device_ts_ns int — the camera's clock when the first frame was taken (GigE, U3V, sim); never a date dropped int — frames lost while it ran: the encoders' queue was full, or the transport lost them dry_run true — with --dry-run; nothing was captured duration_s float — first to last frame, for several ends_at string — with --dry-run, for a time lapse every_s float — with --dry-run, for a time lapse files [string] — absolute paths, in order; at most 1000, the rest counted in truncated first_at string — with --dry-run and --at/--in first_id int — a burst's first frame's block ID format png|jpg|raw — with --dry-run fps float — frames per second from the first frame to the last, by the camera's clock when it has one frames int — frames the camera delivered while the capture ran, including those let pass gaps int — block IDs missing between a burst's first and last frame height int incomplete int — frames that arrived incomplete, where the transport counts them inspect {exposure,verdict,suggest?,focus?,preview?} — with --inspect: the last frame measured as inspect measures it job {id,camera,kind:capture|record|auto,state:armed|running|stopping|done|failed|cancelled|interrupted|lost,saved,planned?,bytes?,last_file?,next_at?,ends_at?,started,ended?,error?:{code,message}} — with --background, as jobs lists it, once armed or its first frame is saved jobs [{id,camera,kind:capture|record|auto,state:armed|running|stopping|done|failed|cancelled|interrupted|lost,saved,planned?,bytes?,last_file?,next_at?,ends_at?,started,ended?,error?:{code,message}}] — with --background and -c repeated last_id int — a burst's last frame's block ID output "-" — with -o -: the image went to stdout passthrough true — the JPEG files are the ones the source sent (an MJPEG webcam, stream or file), as they were, with the provenance comment: not decoded and encoded again pixel_format string — the camera's PFNC format resent int — packets the camera sent again, where the transport counts them settings {exposure_us?,auto_exposure?,gain_db?,gain?,auto_gain?,auto_wb?,fps?,trigger?,black_level?,gamma?,binning?,offset_x?,offset_y?,reverse_x?,reverse_y?} — the camera's settings when the first frame was taken, as the camera has them; trigger: off, or its source (software, line0) settled false — its exposure was still changing when --warmup ran out (with a warning) skew_ms int — with -c repeated: how far apart the cameras' first frames arrived; all were armed first and asked for a frame at the same moment source_bits int — the camera's bits per sample, when the files keep fewer (color or Bayer PNG, JPEG) time string — RFC 3339 time of the first frame truncated int — files saved but not listed warmup_ms int — how long a camera that sets its own exposure took to settle after it started warnings [string] width int Errors: usage , failed , exists , storage_full , frame_timeout , trigger_timeout , interrupted , incomplete , invalid_duration , feature_not_found , out_of_range , unsupported , camera_not_found , camera_ambiguous , camera_busy , disconnected , session_not_found , unavailable , timeout . capturefab record Record video to a file or stream it to rtsp://, srt://, rtmp:// or udp://. Effect: file_write . capturefab record arguments Argument or option Meaning Details -c , --camera CAM Camera ID, serial, IP address, stream URL, file path or simulator (sim:0) env CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA -o , --output FILE|URL A file (.mkv, .mp4, .mov, .ts, .webm; it must not exist, or use {seq}) or a stream URL (rtsp://, srt://, rtmp://, udp://) required --for DUR Stop after this long; without it, record until Ctrl-C (or jobs stop with --background) — --fps N Frames per second written (default: the camera's frame rate); re-encodes a source that would be copied — --codec CODEC h264, hevc or av1 (where a hardware encoder has them), or ffv1 (lossless, .mkv). documents.title: Presets
documents.summary: Save a camera's settings on this computer and restore them as one change.
documents.body: Presets Save a camera's settings on this computer and restore them as one change. capturefab preset Saved camera settings (host-side, portable between cameras of a model). A preset lives on this computer and can be applied to any camera of the model; a user set (exec 'UserSetSave[UserSet1]', or preset apply --persist) lives in the camera. capturefab preset save bench -c sim:0 capturefab preset apply bench -c sim:0 --dry-run capturefab preset list capturefab preset apply Restore a preset as one camera change; a failure puts every value back. Effect: camera_write . capturefab preset apply arguments Argument or option Meaning Details [NAME] — -c , --camera CAM Camera ID, serial, IP address, stream URL, file path or simulator (sim:0) env CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA --file FILE Apply a preset document from a file instead of a saved preset — --dry-run Show what would change, disruptive changes included; change nothing — --strict Fail, changing nothing, if any saved value cannot be applied to this camera — --allow-other-model Apply to a camera of another model; only settings both share change — --persist USERSET Then save it in the camera's user set (default UserSet1) and make that the power-on default — --keep DUR Keep the camera open in a session after use (default 60s). Use 0 to reuse an open session or run without one env CAPTUREFAB_KEEP capturefab preset apply bench -c sim:0 --dry-run capturefab preset apply bench -c sim:0 capturefab preset apply --file bench.json -c sim:0 --strict capturefab preset apply bench -c gige:00c0df123456 --persist UserSet1 capturefab preset apply JSON result Field Type and meaning applied int — values written auto_change {current:bool,saved:bool,action:enter|release|none,risk} — Capturefab auto mode now and in the preset auto_changed bool camera {id,vendor,model,serial} — the camera compared changes [{feature,at?,saved,current,risk:reversible|disruptive,stream_locked,warning?}] — disruptive changes may change triggering, I/O lines or acquisition rate dry_run true — with --dry-run: nothing was written match same_camera|same_model|other_model|unknown_source matched [{feature,at?,value}] not_applied [{feature,at?,status,saved,reason}] persist {user_set,default} — with --dry-run --persist: the user set it would save persisted {user_set,default} — with --persist preset string — the preset's name restarted_stream bool restarts_stream bool — a running stream stops and starts once risk reversible|disruptive — the whole change unchanged int — values that already match warnings [string] Errors: usage , failed , unsupported , out_of_range , invalid_choice , not_writable , feature_locked , camera_not_found , camera_busy , unavailable , timeout . capturefab preset export Write a preset's document to a file, or to stdout. Effect: file_write . capturefab preset export arguments Argument or option Meaning Details NAME — -o , --output FILE The file to write; it must not exist — capturefab preset export bench -o bench.json capturefab preset export bench > bench.json capturefab preset export JSON result Field Type and meaning auto {} — without -o: Capturefab auto mode, when saved on camera {transport,vendor,model,serial?,kind} — without -o name string — without -o note string — without -o path string — with -o: the file written preset string — with -o: the preset's name saved_at string — without -o skipped [{feature,at?,reason}] — without -o values [{feature,value,at?:[{selector,value}]}] — without -o version int — without -o: the document itself, as preset show prints it Errors: usage , failed , exists , storage_full , camera_not_found , unsupported . capturefab preset import Save a preset document from a file, such as one preset export wrote. Effect: file_write . capturefab preset import arguments Argument or option Meaning Details FILE — --name NAME Save it under this name instead of the one in the file — --replace Overwrite a saved preset with the same name — capturefab preset import bench.json capturefab preset import bench.json --name bench2 capturefab preset import JSON result Field Type and meaning camera string — the camera read (save) preset {name,camera,values,skipped,saved_at,path} — values is a count Errors: usage , failed , exists , storage_full , camera_not_found , unsupported . capturefab preset list List saved presets and the folder that holds them. Effect: read . capturefab preset list capturefab --json preset list capturefab preset list JSON result Field Type and meaning dir string — the folder that holds presets presets [{name,transport?,vendor,model,serial?,saved_at,values,note?,status?:unreadable|newer_version,reason?}] — values is a count Errors: usage , failed , camera_not_found , camera_ambiguous , camera_busy , permission_denied , disconnected , auth_required , auth_rejected , session_not_found , ffmpeg_missing , unavailable , timeout . capturefab preset rm Delete a saved preset; no camera changes. Effect: file_write . capturefab preset rm arguments Argument or option Meaning Details NAME — capturefab preset rm bench capturefab --json preset rm bench capturefab preset rm JSON result Field Type and meaning removed string — the preset's name Errors: usage , failed , camera_not_found , camera_ambiguous , camera_busy , permission_denied , disconnected , auth_required , auth_rejected , session_not_found , ffmpeg_missing , unavailable , timeout . capturefab preset save Save the camera's current settings as a named preset. Effect: file_write . capturefab preset save arguments Argument or option Meaning Details NAME — -c , --camera CAM Camera ID, serial, IP address, stream URL, file path or simulator (sim:0) env CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA --note NOTE A short note, such as the lighting it was tuned for — --replace Overwrite a saved preset with the same name — --keep DUR Keep the camera open in a session after use (default 60s). Use 0 to reuse an open session or run without one env CAPTUREFAB_KEEP capturefab preset save bench -c sim:0 capturefab preset save line1 -c gige:00c0df123456 --note 'ring light 60%' capturefab preset save JSON result Field Type and meaning camera string — the camera read (save) preset {name,camera,values,skipped,saved_at,path} — values is a count Errors: usage , failed , exists , storage_full , camera_not_found , unsupported . capturefab preset show Show a saved preset's values. Effect: read . capturefab preset show arguments Argument or option Meaning Details NAME — capturefab preset show bench capturefab --json preset show bench capturefab preset show JSON result Field Type and meaning auto {} — Capturefab auto mode, when saved on camera {transport,vendor,model,serial?,kind} name string note string saved_at string — RFC 3339 skipped [{feature,at?,reason}] values [{feature,value,at?:[{selector,value}]}] version int — document version Errors: usage , failed , camera_not_found , camera_ambiguous , camera_busy , permission_denied , disconnected , auth_required , auth_rejected , session_not_found , ffmpeg_missing , unavailable , timeout .

documents.title: Sessions and jobs
documents.summary: Keep cameras open between commands and run captures and recordings in the background.
documents.body: Sessions and jobs Keep cameras open between commands and run captures and recordings in the background. capturefab session Sessions keep cameras open between commands: start one in the background, stop it, see it. Camera commands can reuse a session that already holds the camera. Most keep the camera open in the auto session for 60s after use. Use --keep DUR to change that time. Use --keep 0 to avoid starting a session for a foreground camera command. Use --no-session to bypass existing sessions. capturefab session start -c sim:0 --live capturefab session status capturefab session stop capturefab session list The running sessions. Effect: read . capturefab session list capturefab --json session list capturefab session list JSON result Field Type and meaning sessions [{session,pid,uptime_s,cameras:[string]}] Errors: usage , failed , session_not_found , unavailable , timeout . capturefab session start Start a session in the background; it ends after --idle unused. Effect: disruptive . capturefab session start arguments Argument or option Meaning Details --name NAME Session name other commands pass to --session default default -c , --camera CAM Camera ID, serial, IP address, stream URL, file path or simulator (sim:0). Repeat for more cameras env CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA ; repeatable --live Keep the cameras streaming, so captures take the newest frame at once — --idle DUR End after this long with no requests and no running jobs default 30m capturefab session start -c sim:0 capturefab session start --name line1 -c gige:00c0df123456 --live --idle 8h capturefab session start JSON result Field Type and meaning cameras [string] — camera IDs it holds log string — where its output goes pid int session string — its name, for --session started bool — false when it was already running warnings [string] Errors: usage , failed , camera_not_found , camera_busy , auth_required , auth_rejected , unavailable , invalid_duration , timeout . capturefab session status A session's cameras, their state and jobs. Effect: read . capturefab session status arguments Argument or option Meaning Details [NAME] The session (default: the only one running) — capturefab session status capturefab --json session status line1 capturefab session status JSON result Field Type and meaning cameras [{id,state:idle|streaming|recording|error,error?:{code,message,hint?,details?:{exit?,signal?,stderr_tail?}},last_error?,config_state?:unknown,frames?,dropped?,lost?,incomplete?,resent?,fps?,jobs:[job]}] — job as jobs lists it; fps: the rate frames arrive at while it streams, by the camera's clock where it stamps them; error: the camera's worker exited (code worker_crashed, with its exit status or signal and last lines of stderr) or did not answer, and the next command on the camera starts another; last_error: the worker's last logged error; lost: frames lost on the way, incomplete: frames the transport received incomplete, resent: packets the camera sent again, where it can tell; config_state unknown: it exited during a settings change, until settings are written again pid int session string uptime_s int Errors: usage , failed , session_not_found , unavailable , timeout . capturefab session stop Stop a session now: its running jobs end as interrupted, keeping the files saved so far. Effect: disruptive . Recordings are finalized. To let jobs finish first, wait for them: capturefab jobs wait ID. capturefab session stop arguments Argument or option Meaning Details [NAME] The session (default: the only one running) — capturefab session stop capturefab session stop line1 capturefab session stop JSON result Field Type and meaning pid int session string stopped bool — true once the process has exited Errors: usage , failed , session_not_found , unavailable , timeout . capturefab serve Run a session in the foreground (systemd, a terminal); Ctrl-C stops it. Effect: disruptive . capturefab serve arguments Argument or option Meaning Details --name NAME Session name other commands pass to --session default default -c , --camera CAM Camera ID, serial, IP address, stream URL, file path or simulator (sim:0). Repeat for more cameras env CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA ; repeatable --live Keep the cameras streaming, so captures take the newest frame at once — capturefab serve --name bench -c sim:0 capturefab serve -c gige:00c0df123456 --live capturefab serve JSON result Field Type and meaning cameras [string] — camera IDs it holds pid int ready bool — printed once the session takes requests session string — its name, for --session Errors: usage , failed , camera_not_found , camera_busy , auth_required , auth_rejected , unavailable , invalid_duration , timeout . capturefab jobs Captures, recordings and auto exposure run in sessions, ended ones included: list, stop, wait. Effect: read . capturefab jobs capturefab jobs wait auto-1 --timeout 10m capturefab jobs stop all capturefab jobs JSON result Field Type and meaning jobs [{id,camera,kind:capture|record|auto,state:armed|running|stopping|done|failed|cancelled|interrupted|lost,saved,planned?,bytes?,last_file?,next_at?,ends_at?,started,ended?,error?:{code,message}}] — every session's, a session that ended included, as it saved them (those that had not ended as lost); finished ones for an hour after they end; with IDs, those jobs in that order; with --running, only those that have not ended Errors: usage , failed , session_not_found , unavailable , timeout . capturefab jobs list Every session's jobs, finished ones and those of ended sessions included; or the jobs named, as they are now. Effect: read . capturefab jobs list arguments Argument or option Meaning Details [ID...] Job IDs such as auto-1: only these, in this order; without waiting, unlike jobs wait — --running Only jobs that have not ended: armed, running or stopping — capturefab jobs list capturefab jobs list --running capturefab --json jobs list auto-1 auto-2 capturefab --json jobs capturefab jobs list JSON result Field Type and meaning jobs [{id,camera,kind:capture|record|auto,state:armed|running|stopping|done|failed|cancelled|interrupted|lost,saved,planned?,bytes?,last_file?,next_at?,ends_at?,started,ended?,error?:{code,message}}] — every session's, a session that ended included, as it saved them (those that had not ended as lost); finished ones for an hour after they end; with IDs, those jobs in that order; with --running, only those that have not ended Errors: usage , failed , session_not_found , unavailable , timeout . capturefab jobs stop Stop a job, or all of them; files saved so far stay. Effect: camera_write . capturefab jobs stop arguments Argument or option Meaning Details ID A job ID such as auto-1, or all — capturefab jobs stop auto-1 capturefab jobs stop all capturefab jobs stop JSON result Field Type and meaning stopped [{id,camera,kind:capture|record|auto,state:armed|running|stopping|done|failed|cancelled|interrupted|lost,saved,planned?,bytes?,last_file?,next_at?,ends_at?,started,ended?,error?:{code,message}}] — the jobs as they are after stopping Errors: usage , failed , session_not_found , unavailable , timeout . capturefab jobs wait Wait for jobs: exit 0 when all are done, a failed one's own code, 4 if one is still running. Effect: read . capturefab jobs wait arguments Argument or option Meaning Details ID... Job IDs such as auto-1; several are waited for together — --timeout DUR How long to wait; none waits until the jobs end default none --progress Report progress on stderr, also without a terminal: a JSON line {progress:{job,camera,kind,state,saved,planned?,bytes?,elapsed_s,left_s?,next_s?}} as the job changes, at least each second — capturefab jobs wait auto-1 capturefab --json jobs wait auto-1 --timeout 10m capturefab --json jobs wait auto-2 auto-3 auto-4 capturefab jobs wait JSON result Field Type and meaning job {id,camera,kind:capture|record|auto,state:armed|running|stopping|done|failed|cancelled|interrupted|lost,saved,planned?,bytes?,last_file?,next_at?,ends_at?,started,ended?,error?:{code,message}} — with one ID: done; a failed job exits with its own error code and details.job jobs [{id,camera,kind:capture|record|auto,state:armed|running|stopping|done|failed|cancelled|interrupted|lost,saved,planned?,bytes?,last_file?,next_at?,ends_at?,started,ended?,error?:{code,message}}] — with several IDs, in the order given, once all have ended: all done; else the first that is not exits with its own error code, and details.jobs holds them all Errors: usage , failed , timeout , interrupted , incomplete , session_not_found , storage_full , frame_timeout , trigger_timeout , exists , unavailable .

documents.title: Sign-ins and networks
documents.summary: Save camera passwords, find ONVIF stream URLs and diagnose GigE connections.
documents.body:
Sign-ins and networks Save camera passwords, find ONVIF stream URLs and diagnose GigE connections. capturefab login Save camera sign-ins for rtsp:// and ONVIF cameras in the OS credential store. printf '%s
' "$PASS" | capturefab login add rtsp://cam.local/stream --user admin --password-stdin capturefab login list capturefab login rm rtsp://cam.local/stream capturefab login add Check a camera sign-in, then save it in the OS credential store. Effect: file_write . capturefab login add arguments Argument or option Meaning Details ADDRESS A credential-free rtsp://, rtsps://, onvif:http://… or onvif://HOST address — --user USER Camera user name — --password-stdin Read the password from stdin (an empty line is an empty password); otherwise CAPTUREFAB_CAMERA_PASSWORD — --no-check Save without connecting to the camera first — printf '%s
' "$PASS" | capturefab login add rtsp://cam.local/stream --user admin --password-stdin printf '%s
' "$PASS" | capturefab login add onvif://cam.local --user admin --password-stdin capturefab login add JSON result Field Type and meaning check {ok,camera} — unless --no-check login {address,user,saved_at} replaced bool Errors: usage , failed , auth_required , auth_rejected , unavailable , unsupported , timeout . capturefab login list List saved camera sign-ins (never their passwords).
